Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE ONE THING THIS SHOP SAYS THAT CHANGES A DIET ANSWER IS ABOUT THE OIL, NOT THE FLOUR: 「胡麻油で揚げる伝統を今に伝える」 — it fries in SESAME OIL, in the old Edo style. That matters twice over. For a coeliac it changes nothing at all: the batter is still wheat flour and the tentsuyu is still soy and dashi, so the whole board is closed. But SESAME is one of Japan’s designated allergens in its own right, and a shop that fries everything in sesame oil is a hazard for a sesame allergy that no dish name would reveal — worth recording because this dataset’s users travel with more than one restriction. ⚠ THERE IS NOTHING HERE FOR EITHER DIET. Every item is battered; 季節の野菜天ぷら at ¥1,940 is six seasonal vegetables and is vegetarian in filling and wheat in coating, which is the same near-miss the vegetable tempura at every other shop in this set produces. ⚠ ONE PRACTICAL NOTE: the 大かき揚 at ¥8,000 is offered but the shop warns 混雑時はお受け出来ない場合もございます — it may be refused at busy times.

Aligot is a 55-seat rustic French place in a 55-year-old wooden house in a Jimbocho backstreet, with standing, tatami and private rooms, run by Yumeya (which also runs a gibier distribution business — hence the wild boar). ⚠ NO ALLERGEN INFORMATION IS PUBLISHED AND FRENCH BISTRO COOKING IS A FLOUR KITCHEN: 煮込みハンバーグ is panko-bound in a flour-thickened sauce, the カスレ carries a house sausage (rusk filler) and is normally crumb-gratinated, and the コロッケ is breaded. アリゴ itself — the Auvergnat potato-and-tomme purée the shop is named for — is potato, cheese, butter and garlic with no flour in the classical recipe, but the shop states no ingredients, so it is ask. The chain caveat 「一部店舗では取り扱いのないメニューがある場合や価格が異なる場合がございます」 applies, hence partial. This is a Jiro-style (二郎系) shop and the numbers matter: 小 is 250 g of noodle, ミニ 125 g, 大 375 g, and the chain warns its own 小 is about the size of an ordinary shop’s 大盛 and tells first-timers to order ミニ or 小. ⚠ NOTHING IN THIS SHOP IS GLUTEN-FREE AND THE FREE-TOPPING RITUAL DOES NOT CHANGE THAT. 極太麺 is thick wheat noodle, the tare is soy, and the pork is soy-braised; the 汁なし, つけ麺 and 冷やし中華 variants are the same noodle with more soy. The chain DOES publish an アレルギー表・産地情報 PDF at https://butayama.com/allergy/ and it IS a real allergen table, but it is a graphical scan whose Japanese product names and marks do not extract as text, so nothing below is drawn from it. ⚠ THE CALL SYSTEM IS THE ONE THING A VISITOR SHOULD PRE-LEARN, and the shop prints the exact quantities: garlic 抜き 0 g / 少し half a tablespoon / ニンニク one tablespoon / マシマシ two tablespoons; vegetables 少なめ 150 g / 標準 300 g / マシ 450 g / マシマシ 600 g; back fat 標準 / アブラ / アブラマシマシ; tare strength 標準 / カラメ / カラカラ. Calls are taken just before the bowl is handed over; 麺硬め must be said earlier, when the ticket is collected. ⚠ SEASONAL LINES: つけ麺 is sold 1 April to 30 September and 冷やし中華 1 June to 30 September only.

tokyo_niku_bistro_akari.price_note: ALMOST EMPTY ON PURPOSE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING. 肉ビストロ灯 (西新宿7-16-3 第18フジビル 2F, Zekkocho group) does publish its full Food, Drink and Course menus — but only as three image-scan PDFs linked from its Menu page (20260217_Food_Menu.pdf, 20260217_Drink_Menu.pdf, course.pdf, all dated by the 2026.02.17 グランドメニューが新しくなりました news item). pdftotext returns one byte from each: they carry no text layer, and this machine has no pdftoppm to render the pages, so NOT ONE DISH NAME OR PRICE COULD BE READ. The single price the site states in HTML is the お通し at 660 yen (税込), recorded below because it is compulsory. What the site does describe in words, and which is worth knowing before booking: the kitchen serves 6-8 different 塊肉 (whole-block cuts) a day — beef, pork, lamb and gibier including venison and wild boar — seared over 備長炭 charcoal and served rare in the middle, alongside a locked wine cellar of roughly 100-150 bottles that guests walk into with a lantern. tokyo_hikiniku_to_come_shibuya.price_note: ⚠ THIS IS THE BEST ALLERGEN DISCLOSURE FOUND IN THIS WHOLE TICK AND IT DELIVERS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT PEOPLE HOPE. 挽肉と米 publishes a real, machine-readable per-item allergen table at hikinikutocome.com/allergen covering all 29 Japanese labelled items, and it declares the HAMBURG ITSELF as containing 卵・牛乳・小麦・牛肉 — WHEAT IS IN THE PATTY. A shop whose entire menu is three charcoal-grilled minced-beef patties and a bowl of rice reads, to a coeliac, like it ought to be safe; it is not, and only the shop’s own table would have told you. The prices are the other half of the story: NO PRICE IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE ON THE OFFICIAL SITE — not on the Shibuya page, not on the menu page, not in the FAQ — so the set below is unpriced, deliberately. ⚠ WHAT IS ACTUALLY SAFE HERE, BY THE SHOP’S OWN TABLE: the 味噌汁 (declares 牛乳・大豆, no wheat), the コッチョリ生キムチ (えび・ごま), the ポテサラ (卵・大豆・りんご・牛肉) and the three table spice blends (ごま only) — BUT read the miso soup line with care, because 麦味噌 is BARLEY and barley is NOT one of the 29 labelled items, so an allergen table CANNOT clear a miso soup of gluten. Everything soy-based is declared wheat: 挽肉のタレ, 食べる醤油 and 生醤油 all list 小麦. ⚠ ONE INCONSISTENCY WORTH KNOWING: the 楽しみ方 page says the set comes with 自家製ポン酢, but ポン酢 does not appear anywhere in the allergen table — ask which of the declared sauces it corresponds to. Format: the menu is deliberately ONE dish, three 90 g patties served one at a time onto rice with free rice refills, one free egg per person, and 鬼おろし grated daikon arriving with the second patty. Shibuya is at 渋谷区道玄坂2-28-1 椎津ビル3F, 11:00-15:00 and 17:00-21:00, closed Wednesdays, walk-in register via web only — no phone or SNS booking. The 八味唐辛子 in the table is marked 京都店のみ and is NOT available at Shibuya.

tokyo_curry_rice_specialist_et.price_note: NO PRICES ARE PUBLISHED on the shop’s own site, which was rebuilt on 2025-07-29 with an お薦めメニュー page that names the dishes and describes them but prints no figures at all — hence partial, and hence unpriced items. カリーライス専門店エチオピア 本店 is the Jimbocho original, founded 1988, owner-chef 鈴木堅司, and the site describes the style as インド風カリーライス. ⚠ THE ALLERGEN PDF EXISTS, DECLARES WHEAT, AND ITS GRID CANNOT BE READ. The shop links food-allergy.pdf and its header states in English that ALL MENU items are covered for «shrimp, wheat, eggs, dairy, cashew nut, beef, soybeans, chicken, banana, pork, yam, lamb, apple, gelatin, sesame». Its text layer is a simple one-character-shifted cipher and the English header decodes cleanly, but the Japanese product names and the per-item marks are CID glyphs that yield nothing, so WHICH dishes contain the wheat could not be established here. ⚠ THAT MATTERS BECAUSE THE SHOP’S OWN PROSE POINTS AT THE ANSWER: every description on the site is built around the ルー — 「ルーとビーフ、そしてライスの織り成す絶妙のバランス」, 「ルーとの相性がすこぶる良く」 — and a Japanese curry ルー is a WHEAT-FLOUR roux. The bean curries are described as サラサラタイプのルー (thin, not thickened), which is the one hint that they may be built differently, but the shop does not say so and it must not be assumed. Every curry is therefore recorded no. The bean curries are also flagged 辛さは3倍から — they START at heat level 3.

tokyo_shibuya_yokocho_hokkaido.price_note: PARTIAL BECAUSE THE OPERATOR PUBLISHES DISHES AND REFUSES TO PUBLISH PRICES, AND SAYS SO. 渋谷横丁 is a nineteen-unit food-and-entertainment strip inside RAYARD MIYASHITA PARK, and its official site gives each unit a block with a description, a phone number, opening hours and a MENU list of named dishes — under a standing caveat printed above every one of them: 「※仕入れ状況によって、メニューや価格が変更となる場合がございます」, menus and prices change with what comes in. No figure appears against any dish anywhere on the site. The twelve dishes below are the ones the operator lists for the HOKKAIDO 食市 unit specifically, not for the strip as a whole. TEL 03-6805-1257, 11:00 to 05:00 the following morning, except Sundays when it closes at 23:00. ⚠ TWO NAMES ON THIS LIST MEAN THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE, AND THE OPERATOR FLAGS BOTH ITSELF. 室蘭焼鳥 is written with the characters for grilled CHICKEN and the site says plainly that in Muroran 「やきとり」 means PORK and onion — the strip's own summary line even reads 「鳥は使わないけど『室蘭焼き鳥』」, 'we don't use chicken, but it's Muroran yakitori'. And 北海道ザンギ is not plain fried chicken: the site says the local way is to eat it dipped in Worcester sauce with pepper floated on it, and WORCESTER SAUCE IS A WHEAT-AND-ANCHOVY PRODUCT, so the sauce is both a gluten fact and a fish fact that the karaage itself would not have told you. ⚠ THE REST IS A HOKKAIDO IZAKAYA BOARD AND THERE IS NOTHING VEGAN ON IT: seafood bowls, crab, sea urchin, squid, mutton-adjacent grills, pork, and a miso ramen. The one non-animal line, ソフトクリーム, is dairy.

tokyo_raishu_ken.price_note: THE WEBSITE THIS DATASET CARRIES IS NO LONGER THE SHOP'S — IT IS A PARKED DOMAIN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. https://www.raisyuken.com/ returns a 4.8KB page whose entire body is the word "Redirecting..." plus an obfuscated script that POSTs to router.parklogic.com, a domain-monetisation service. Decoding the script's own base64 configuration confirms it: it declares domainFull "www.raisyuken.com" under tenant "seth", i.e. the domain has been picked up by a parking operator. There is no restaurant content at this address at all — no menu, no address block, no hours, no navigation. Re-fetching will not help; the record needs a NEW first-party URL before it can be researched, and until it has one it is not reachable work. The dataset's menu_url points at Tabelog, which this egress cannot reach (Cloudflare challenge since 2026-09-02). 来集軒 is recorded here as a 醤油ラーメン shop in Asakusa — soy-sauce ramen is wheat noodles in a soy tare, so the whole proposition is gluten, but no dish or price has been established.

tokyo_izakaya_todoroki_asakusa.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own HotPepper page (台東区浅草1-1-16 HK浅草ビル5階 — the record's Asakusa-ekimae placement). Unusually for this operator the shop writes its whole card in Japanese AND English, so a traveller can read it unaided at the table; the English is the shop's own. ⚠ THE BURIED ITEM ON THIS CARD IS 十割そば AT ¥858, and it is the classic Japanese gluten trap: 十割 means the noodle itself is 100% buckwheat with no wheat cut into the dough, which is exactly why people mistake it for safe — but the board it is cut on is dusted with wheat 打ち粉, and the tsuyu it is dipped in is wheat soy sauce. A coeliac should not read 十割 as an all-clear. ⚠ Second trap, and it is regional: the shop bills itself Hakata/Kyushu, and its 博多もつ鍋 broth is described as a house miso soup. Kyushu miso is traditionally 麦味噌 — BARLEY — which is gluten and which Japan's statutory allergen labelling does not cover at all, so a 小麦 column reading clear tells you nothing here. The 牛すじ煮込み is miso-simmered on the same logic, and the 辛子れんこん is a Kumamoto dish whose stuffing is a mustard miso. ⚠ The 野菜巻き串 section reads vegetable but every single skewer is a vegetable WRAPPED IN PORK — lettuce, tomato, spring onion, shiitake, enoki, asparagus. There is no vegetable-only skewer on the card. For a vegan the only candidates are 枝豆, やみつき旨キャベツ, 冷やしトマト and ひややっこ, and the cabbage is dressed in a garlic-salt sesame dressing and the tofu is topped with condiments and normally soy.

tokyo_touka_motsunabe_to_shoch.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own HotPepper page at 渋谷区道玄坂1-11-3 フォースワンビル2F — which matches the record's Dogenzaka placement, two minutes from Shibuya south exit. ⚠ NAME AND CONCEPT HAVE MOVED. The record calls this 「もつ鍋と焼酎のお店 とうか」; the shop's own live page is titled 「薬膳火鍋 居酒屋 とうか 渋谷」 — a medicinal-herb hotpot izakaya. Same address and same phone, so it is the same business rather than a different one, but a traveller arriving expecting a motsunabe-and-shochu specialist will find a broad izakaya card, and NO もつ鍋 appears anywhere on the current 料理 list. The nearest thing is 和牛もつラーメン. Treat the record's cuisine label as stale. ⚠ The card is unusually WIDE — sashimi, grilled offal, natto, pizza, omelettes, Chinese stir-fries and ramen on one page — and the gluten is scattered accordingly rather than concentrated: everything in 【揚】 is fried, the three ピザ are wheat bases, 豚肉焼きそば is a wheat noodle, 和牛もつラーメン is a wheat noodle in a miso or soy broth, and every 麻姿 (mapo) and チリソース dish is thickened and soy-seasoned. ⚠ 納豆 gets its own section of five dishes, which is rare and genuinely useful for a vegan — but packaged natto ships with a soy-sauce sachet, so ask for it without the tare. The 豆腐 section is the other plant-leaning corner.

tokyo_qipo_chuanchuanxiang.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own site. ⚠ BRANCH CHECK: the record carries no branch suffix but the page is 「七婆串串香 渋谷店」 at 渋谷区神宮前6-19-17 GEMS神宮前 8F, which matches the record's Miyamasuzaka/Jingumae placement. ⚠ THIS IS A SICHUAN SKEWER HOT POT AND THE STRUCTURE IS ITS OWN HAZARD: you pick a broth, then everything else on the card goes into that one shared pot. So a single wheat item in the basket contaminates every skewer anybody dips afterwards, and this card has several — the 野菜 platter at ¥660 explicitly bundles ラーメン and 刀削麺 (wheat noodles) together with 餅巾着 and 湯葉, and 板春雨 and 干し豆腐 sit in the same tray as 麺. For a coeliac the only workable approach here is a dedicated pot with a chosen, checked basket, which is a conversation to have before ordering. ⚠ THE BROTHS: 麻辣 is built on doubanjiang, which is a broad-bean paste very commonly fermented with WHEAT flour, and Sichuan hot-pot bases routinely include soy and fermented black bean. 漢方白湯 is a herbal pork-bone milk broth, きのこ is mushroom, トマト is tomato — the last two are the most plausible non-wheat and non-animal bases but the shop publishes no ingredient list for any of them. ⚠ VEGAN: the 【串】-野菜- rows are genuinely plant — mushrooms, lotus root, bamboo, corn, yam, konnyaku, broccoli, tofu skin — at ¥99 a skewer, which makes this one of the cheaper plant-heavy cards in the dataset. But ちくわ in that same vegetable row is a fish cake, and the pot itself is shared with meat.

items.note: ⚠ The wheat is here. ラーメン and 刀削麺 are both wheat noodles and they are bundled onto the SAME plate as the mochi and tofu skin, which then goes into the shared pot. This one ¥660 line is the reason a coeliac cannot share a pot at this shop.

items.ja: えびのつみれ、ゼンマイ、鴨の腸等
items.romaji: ebi no tsumire, zenmai, kamo no chō nado
items.en: Prawn balls, fern shoots and duck intestine
items.note: つみれ prawn balls are bound with wheat starch or flour as standard.

items.ja: 鶏肉団子／砂肝／せせり／豚の大腸
items.romaji: toriniku dango / sunagimo / seseri / buta no daichō
items.en: Chicken meatball, gizzard, neck and pork large intestine skewers
items.note: The 鶏肉団子 meatball is flour- or starch-bound; the rest are plain meat but share the pot with it.

items.ja: 豚の軟骨／鶏もも／広東ソーセージ／四川風牛肉巻
items.romaji: buta no nankotsu / tori momo / Kanton sōsēji / Shisen-fū gyūniku maki
items.en: Pork cartilage, chicken thigh, Cantonese sausage and Sichuan-style beef roll skewers
items.note: Cantonese lap cheong is cured with soy sauce and rice wine; the Sichuan beef roll is pre-marinated.

items.ja: 豆苗の牛肉巻／パクチーの牛肉巻／えのきの牛肉巻
items.romaji: tōmyō no gyūniku maki / pakuchī no gyūniku maki / enoki no gyūniku maki
items.en: Pea shoot, coriander or enoki rolled in beef
items.note: Vegetable wrapped in beef — reads plant, is meat.

items.ja: 七婆特製牛肉／手羽中／牛のハチノス／マーラー牛肉／アヒルのハツモト
items.romaji: Qipo tokusei gyūniku / tebanaka / gyū no hachinosu / mārā gyūniku / ahiru no hatsumoto
items.en: House-seasoned beef, chicken mid-wing, beef honeycomb tripe, mala beef and duck aorta skewers
items.note: The 特製 and マーラー beef are pre-marinated in the shop's own seasoning, which is not published and in Sichuan cooking is soy- and doubanjiang-based.

items.ja: 海老団子／イカ団子／牛肉団子／ほら貝
items.romaji: ebi dango / ika dango / gyūniku dango / horagai
items.en: Prawn ball, squid ball, beef ball and conch skewers
items.note: Every 団子 ball on this row is bound with wheat starch or flour as standard.

items.ja: 魚豆腐／海老／白身魚／魚卵入り魚肉団子
items.romaji: gyodōfu / ebi / shiromizakana / gyoran-iri gyoniku dango
items.en: Fish tofu, prawn, white fish and roe-filled fish ball skewers
items.note: 魚豆腐 fish tofu is a surimi product, not bean curd, and both it and the fish balls are starch-and-flour bound.

items.ja: ちくわ／かぼちゃ／とうもろこし／きくらげ
items.en: Chikuwa fish cake, pumpkin, sweetcorn and wood-ear mushroom skewers
items.note: ⚠ ちくわ is filed under VEGETABLES here and it is a fish cake bound with wheat starch. The pumpkin, corn and wood-ear on the same row are plant and clean in themselves.

items.ja: れんこんの薄切り／しいたけ／しめじ
items.en: Sliced lotus root, shiitake and shimeji skewers
items.note: Plain vegetables and mushrooms with nothing added — plant-based. The gluten question is the shared pot, not the skewer.

items.ja: エリンギ／山芋／干し豆腐
items.en: King oyster mushroom, mountain yam and dried tofu-sheet skewers
items.note: Plant-based. 干し豆腐 is pressed soy bean curd, not a wheat noodle, despite sitting near the noodle plate on the card.

items.ja: 厚揚げ／筍の先／じゃがいもの薄切り
items.romaji: atsuage / takenoko no saki / jagaimo no usugiri
items.en: Fried tofu, bamboo shoot tips and sliced potato skewers
items.note: Plant-based; the atsuage is pre-fried at the tofu maker rather than in this kitchen.

items.ja: うずらの卵／ブロッコリー／こんにゃく
items.en: Quail egg, broccoli and konnyaku skewers
items.note: The quail egg makes this row non-vegan; broccoli and konnyaku on their own are plant.

items.ja: 筍の薄切り／豆苗豆腐皮／えのき豆皮巻き／冬瓜
items.romaji: takenoko no usugiri / tōmyō tōfugawa / enoki tōhi maki / tōgan
items.en: Sliced bamboo shoot, pea shoots in tofu skin, enoki rolled in tofu skin and winter melon skewers
items.note: All-plant, and the tofu-skin wraps are soy rather than wheat — worth knowing, because a rolled skewer usually means pastry or meat. Shared pot remains the issue.

tokyo_grill_grand.price_note: ⚠ THIRTEEN DISHES AND NOT ONE PRICE. Tabelog lists the full carte for グリル グランド — six meat dishes, four seafood, two starters and a sandwich — and prints no figure against any of them, with no 更新日 either. So this record is a reliable DISH LIST and no kind of price guide. The only monetary evidence on the page is the recorded average spend, and it is startling: 10,000–14,999円 at dinner against 3,000–3,999円 at lunch. A three-to-four-fold gap between services at the same Asakusa yoshoku room is the single most practical fact available about this shop — go at lunch, or budget properly. ⚠ YOSHOKU IS THE MOST WHEAT-DENSE CUISINE IN JAPAN AND THIS MENU IS A DEMONSTRATION OF WHY. Japanese Western-style cooking is built on two things a coeliac cannot have: ドミグラスソース, a sauce thickened with a long-cooked WHEAT-FLOUR roux, which is what goes over the beef stew, the braised hamburg and most of the sautés; and パン粉, breadcrumb, which is what goes round the beef cutlet, the crab cream croquette and the katsu sandwich. The gratin adds a third, béchamel, which is flour and milk. Working down the thirteen lines, there is no dish that is plausibly wheat-free — not one — and the shop publishes no allergen information. ⚠ THERE IS ALSO NOTHING MEAT-FREE OR FISH-FREE. Every one of the thirteen items names an animal in its own title: beef six times, pork once, prawn, crab, squid, oyster. A vegetarian has no entry point to this menu at all, and that is worth stating flatly rather than leaving to be inferred from thirteen separate "no" marks. ⭐ ONE LINE DEFEATS ALL THREE TRANSLATIONS AND IS RECORDED AS UNKNOWN RATHER THAN GUESSED. The ninth item renders as "Panko Katsu" in English, as 麵包可可 — literally "bread cocoa" — in Chinese, and as a garbled transliteration in Korean. Three machine translations failing in three different directions means the underlying Japanese is something none of them parsed, and since it sits in the SEAFOOD section it is most likely a crumbed fish dish. It is filed below with the name unresolved, because inventing a plausible Japanese string for it would put a dish in this dataset that may not exist. ON THE SHOP: 浅草3-24-6, 50 seats with 20 at tables on the ground floor and private rooms upstairs, lunch from 11:30, closed MONDAYS AND SUNDAYS — a two-day weekend closure that catches visitors, since most Asakusa restaurants trade on Sunday.

items.en: Beef sauté
items.note: BEEF. Marked ask rather than no only because a sauté is the one preparation on this list that COULD arrive without a flour-thickened sauce — but at a yoshoku counter the pan is almost always finished with demi-glace or a soy-butter, and both carry wheat. Ask what the sauce is.

items.en: Beef tenderloin cutlet — fillet crumbed and deep-fried
items.note: ⚠ カツ＝パン粉＝小麦。BEEF in BREADCRUMB. カツ always means panko-crumbed and deep-fried, so the word itself is the gluten warning. Shares a fryer with the prawn and crab dishes.

items.en: Beef tenderloin steak
items.note: BEEF. The plainest cooking on the menu and therefore the best gluten prospect of the thirteen — a steak is meat and heat. ⚠ But the sauce beside it is the question, and at a yoshoku grill that sauce is conventionally demi-glace, i.e. a WHEAT roux. Ask for it plain or on the side.

items.en: Beef stew — the long-braised yoshoku standard
items.note: ⚠ ドミグラスソース＝小麦粉のルウ。BEEF in a demi-glace, and demi-glace is a sauce built on a ROUX OF WHEAT FLOUR cooked for hours. This is the definitional yoshoku gluten dish — the wheat is dissolved into the sauce, invisible, and there is no version of the dish without it. Also usually finished with red wine and butter (DAIRY).

items.ja: 煮込みビーフハンバーグ
items.en: Beef hamburg steak braised in sauce
items.note: ⚠ TWO SEPARATE WHEAT SOURCES. A Japanese ハンバーグ is bound with PANKO and milk inside the patty, and this one is then braised in a demi-glace, which is a flour roux — so the wheat is in the meat as well as around it. BEEF, EGG (standard binder) and DAIRY.

items.ja: プラチナポークのステーキ
items.en: Platinum Pork steak — a branded pork, the only non-beef meat on the list
items.note: PORK. プラチナポーク is a brand name for a specific producer's pork rather than a cut or a grade — worth knowing so it is not mistaken for a quality classification like 黒毛和牛. Same sauce caveat as the beef steak: ask before assuming the plate arrives without a flour-thickened sauce.

items.en: Deep-fried kuruma prawn — the large Japanese tiger prawn, crumbed
items.note: ⚠ PRAWN, a statutory allergen, in PANKO. 車海老 is the premium Japanese prawn, so this is likely to be among the dearer plates on an unpriced menu. It is also the dish that contaminates the fryer for everything else in this section.

items.ja: カニクリームコロッケ
items.en: Crab cream croquette
items.note: ⚠ WHEAT TWICE AND TWO ALLERGENS. The filling is a BÉCHAMEL — flour cooked in butter and milk — and the coating is PANKO, so there is wheat inside and outside. CRAB (statutory allergen) and DAIRY. One of the most reliably impossible dishes in Japanese cooking for a coeliac.

items.ja: （名称未確定：英「Panko Katsu」／中「麵包可可」）
items.en: A crumbed cutlet in the seafood section whose Japanese name could not be recovered — see note
items.note: ⚠ RECORDED AS UNKNOWN ON PURPOSE. All three Tabelog locales garble this line differently — English gives the non-name "Panko Katsu", Chinese gives 麵包可可 ("bread cocoa"), Korean gives an unparseable transliteration — which means none of them resolved the underlying Japanese, and there is no way to recover it from this source. Its SECTION is solid evidence, though: it sits among the seafood, and パン粉カツ means crumbed and fried. So: assume FISH or shellfish, assume PANKO, assume WHEAT. The name needs a first-party source or a photograph to settle and should not be guessed at.

items.ja: グラタン（海老・蟹からお選びください。※冬季限定で牡蠣グラタンもあります）
items.romaji: guratan (ebi / kani kara o-erabi kudasai; tōki gentei de kaki guratan mo arimasu)
items.en: Gratin — choose prawn or crab; an oyster gratin is also available in winter only
items.note: ⚠ THREE STATUTORY ALLERGENS IN ONE LINE AND A WHEAT SAUCE UNDER ALL OF THEM. PRAWN, CRAB and — seasonally — OYSTER, over a BÉCHAMEL, which is wheat flour and milk. ⭐ Note the winter-only oyster version: this is the one item on the menu that tells you the kitchen changes with the season, and it is the reason to ask what else is 冬季限定 when you visit.

items.en: Wagyu tataki — seared outside, raw within, sliced thin as a starter
items.note: BEEF, and RAW in the middle — たたき means the surface only is seared. The one starter with a real chance of being wheat-free, since it is meat and a dressing; ⚠ but that dressing is conventionally 醤油-based (WHEAT) or a ponzu, which is also soy. Ask.

items.ja: ミニヤリイカのガーリックソテー
items.en: Small spear squid sautéed with garlic
items.note: SQUID, a declarable allergen in Japan and easy to miss in an English menu. ヤリイカ is spear squid specifically. A garlic sauté is oil, garlic and squid, so this is arguably the least wheat-laden plate on the whole menu — marked ask rather than yes because yoshoku kitchens finish garlic sautés with soy or butter as a matter of habit.

items.en: Beef cutlet sandwich
items.note: ⚠ WHEAT THREE TIMES OVER — the BREAD, the PANKO on the cutlet, and the sauce, which for a katsu sando is a Worcester-style sauce that normally contains wheat. BEEF. If a single item could stand for why yoshoku is hard for a coeliac, it is this one.
